rules.statement: When rotating a refresh token, revoke the presented grant and store its successor in a single unit of work, conditional on the presented grant still being active.
rules.why: If the spend and the successor store happen in separate units of work, concurrent refreshes can both get tokens, or a lineage revocation can run between the two steps and leave the successor active.
rules.check: Look for refresh-token rotation code that revokes the old grant and saves the new grant in separate SaveChanges/unit-of-work calls, or uses an idempotent revoke that succeeds even when the grant is already revoked.

rules.statement: Treat a refresh request that loses the race to spend a rotated refresh token (grant missing, not active, or the save hit a concurrency conflict) as a reuse: return invalid_grant (400), emit the replay audit event, and apply the configured reuse policy such as revoking the lineage.
rules.why: The server can't tell the attacker from the client, so RFC 9700 §4.14.2 requires the losing request to be treated as reuse, not answered with a 500 or allowed to succeed.
rules.check: Look for a failed or lost spend of a refresh token that throws a 500, gets ignored, or still issues tokens instead of taking the reuse/replay path.

rules.statement: In a refresh-token grant handler, spend the presented refresh token only after every validation (token, binding, request) and before minting or auditing any access token, ID token, or successor token.
rules.why: If tokens are minted before the spend and the spend is then lost, the server has minted and audited tokens that are never delivered.
rules.check: Look for access/ID token creation or issuance auditing that happens before the refresh token is spent, or a spend that runs before validation finishes.

rules.statement: Spend a rotated refresh token by revoking it, not just marking it consumed, so it is unusable to introspection, revocation, and listing.
rules.why: A consumed grant still reads as active to introspection, revocation, and listing, while a revoked grant is unusable everywhere.
rules.check: Look for rotation that sets only a consumed timestamp on the presented grant and does not revoke it.

rules.statement: When a revocation of a set of related grants (such as a refresh-token lineage) loses an optimistic-concurrency race, read the set again and retry a bounded number of times rather than failing or skipping.
rules.why: A rotation that committed in between may have added a grant to the set, and a revocation that doesn't retry would leave that grant active.
rules.check: Look for a lineage or bulk revocation that catches a concurrency exception and gives up, rethrows, or retries without re-reading the set, or that retries without a limit.

rules.statement: A non-critical update such as a sliding-expiration extension must tolerate losing an optimistic-concurrency race by keeping the other request's change instead of throwing.
rules.why: Another concurrent request already updated the row, so throwing would only turn a harmless race into an error.
rules.check: Look for sliding-expiration or similar best-effort updates whose concurrency conflict propagates as an exception.
